papers.title: BrainCodes: A Lightweight EEG Foundation Model over Discrete Neural Codes
papers.summary: Introduces BrainCodes, a lightweight EEG foundation model pretrained via self-supervised learning on over 800 hours of recordings from more than 1,000 participants, combining a quantization-based neural tokenizer with a spatiotemporal encoder supporting arbitrary electrode configurations. It matches or surpasses state-of-the-art performance on sleep staging, attention assessment, and cognitive load estimation while using up to 97% fewer trainable parameters, and transfers to low-resource wearable devices.

papers.title: NED-Net: an annotation-training loop for rodent EEG event detection
papers.summary: Introduces NED-Net, open-source software that trains and continuously retrains rodent seizure detectors using reviewed candidate events as labels. A detector across cohorts went from mostly-seizure detections with low per-animal recall to, after cohort-specific retraining, convulsive recall of 64% (up from 15%) with at least one reference seizure in every animal.

papers.title: Subject-independent classification of ADHD from pediatric EEG: a leakage-aware deep learning framework with interpretable neurophysiological mapping.
papers.summary: Compared classical ML and deep learning models for pediatric ADHD EEG classification under segment-wise versus leakage-free subject-wise cross-validation; SVM on power spectral density features fell from 90.0% to 65.6% accuracy, while a raw-EEG CNN retained 72.7% on unseen participants, with SHAP attributions highlighting frontal (F3, Fz, F4) and central (Cz) electrodes.

papers.title: Enhancing cortical electrophysiological signatures of sleep overrides ER stress responses in sleep-deprived mice
papers.summary: In sleep-deprived mice, flickering light stimulation during deprivation prevented upregulation of activity-dependent and unfolded protein response (ER stress) genes while further increasing NREM slow-wave activity, and induced brief neuronal OFF periods resembling sleep-like cortical states. The authors conclude that physiological manipulation of cortical activity can dissociate molecular ER-stress signatures from electrophysiological sleep-pressure markers.

papers.title: Portable polysomnography-derived multi-domain EEG markers of anesthetic state transitions during propofol anesthesia for gastrointestinal endoscopy.
papers.summary: In a prospective observational study of 31 adults undergoing propofol-based gastrointestinal endoscopy, portable polysomnography-derived six-channel EEG captured stage-related changes across baseline, induction, maintenance, and recovery, including decreasing relative delta power, increasing theta/alpha/sigma/beta power and SEF95, and highest spindle-like event density during recovery. Amplitude envelope correlation showed the most widespread stage-related connectivity differences, identifying candidate EEG markers for emergence detection and atypical anesthetic-state identification.

papers.title: The Metrology Atlas: describing recorded physiological data as a measurement system, with VitalDB as a first application
papers.summary: Presents the Metrology Atlas, a dataset-independent framework describing recorded physiological data as a measurement system, applied as a proof of principle to VitalDB (6,388 surgical patients) with evidence-tagged measurement models, a mapped timing network of 11 clocks and 14 devices, and documented data-quality issues. Synchronization reduced median timing error between EEG and ECG from 794 ms to 42 ms and between ventilator and monitor waveforms from 378 ms to 55 ms.

papers.title: Associations Between Biomarkers of Alzheimer's Disease and Sleep in Cognitively Unimpaired Older Adults.
papers.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
papers.summary: Examined associations between plasma Alzheimer's disease biomarkers and polysomnographic sleep macro/microstructure in 40 cognitively unimpaired older adults, finding that higher amyloid-β concentrations were associated with shorter and less dense sleep spindles and lower alpha, beta, and spindle-frequency EEG power, while higher t-tau and p-tau181 related to reduced N3 sleep and longer nocturnal wakefulness.

papers.title: Multi-Metric EEG Connectivity and Graph Analysis Reveal Altered Resting-State Networks in Major Depressive Disorder.
papers.summary: Applied multi-metric resting-state EEG connectivity (coherence, PLV, PLI, mutual information) and graph analysis in 30 MDD participants and 28 controls, reporting predominantly lower theta/alpha connectivity across distributed sensor pairs alongside increased beta mutual-information dependence and lower theta/alpha weighted strength and global efficiency.

papers.title: MULTIMODAL EEG WORLD MODEL: SELF-SUPERVISED LATENT TRANSITION LEARNING FOR WEARABLE EEG SEIZURE DETECTION
papers.summary: The authors propose a self-supervised Multimodal EEG World Model that predicts the latent representation of the next EEG segment conditioned on synchronized ECG, EMG, and movement signals via query-based fusion, with label-free pretraining and a frozen encoder plus linear probe downstream. On SeizeIT2 with a strict patient-wise split it achieved AUPRC 0.3748, ROC-AUC 0.8025, and balanced accuracy 0.7308, outperforming database and external baselines and showing a 14.4% relative AUPRC gain over a random-initialized encoder.

papers.title: MSANet: a multi-scale spatiotemporal adaptive network for EEG-based driver fatigue recognition.
papers.summary: Proposed MSANet, a multi-scale spatiotemporal adaptive network with multi-granularity temporal gating, graph-node enhancement, and adaptive classifier gating, for cross-subject EEG driver fatigue recognition, achieving 83.64% accuracy/F1 83.74 on Dataset I and 74.64% accuracy/F1 72.92 on Dataset II.

papers.title: Daytime Napping and Associative-Memory Retrieval Speed: An Exploratory Behavioral and EEG Study
papers.summary: In a within-participant exploratory study of 15 healthy students, daytime napping was associated with 6.7% faster delayed associative recognition (significant Condition-by-Time interaction, b = -0.063, p = .027) while monitored wakefulness produced no change, with the difference concentrated among slower responses; accuracy did not differ by condition. Nap EEG showed aperiodic spectral slowing and stronger periodic sigma activity, but no EEG measure explained the response-time effect.

papers.title: A brain-behavior generative model links individual brain dynamics to perceptual decisions
papers.summary: Introduces a brain-behavior generative model in which whole-brain dynamics on each participant's structural connectome generate both single-trial EEG and reaction times, fitted to 17 participants performing motion discrimination. The models reproduced individual event-related potentials and reaction-time distributions and predicted held-out trial speed, while in silico silencing showed sensorimotor regions consistently affected decision speed but the same parietal region had opposite effects across participants.

papers.title: Auditory sustained potential as a biomarker of language functioning in children with autism and its implication in clinical trials.
papers.summary: In an open-label pilot study of 19 children with autism, the auditory sustained potential (SP) amplitude was reduced at baseline and correlated with language scores; probiotic supplementation increased SP negativity and improved language scores, suggesting SP as a potential biomarker for clinical trials.

papers.title: An attention-enhanced hybrid CNN-BiLSTM framework for multiclass epileptic seizure recognition using EEG signals.
papers.summary: Developed a CNN-BiLSTM-MHSA hybrid deep learning framework for multiclass epileptic seizure recognition on 11,500 EEG segments, reporting 98.83% accuracy, 98.90% F1-score, and 99.80% ROC-AUC and outperforming several recent state-of-the-art EEG seizure classifiers.

papers.title: Inter-subject correlations and their behavioral associations vary across movies: Implications for generalizability.
papers.summary: Analyzing three datasets (318 subjects, 36 movies), this study found that inter-subject correlation (ISC) and ISC-behavior associations vary substantially across movies, with little overlap in spatial patterns, indicating that ISC findings may be movie-specific and challenging to generalize.

papers.title: Diaphragm 'atonia' during ictal and post-ictal apnoea: A case report.
papers.summary: A case report of a 26-year-old with temporal lobe epilepsy using video-EEG polygraphy with surface EMG showed diaphragmatic and intercostal muscle silence during ictal and post-ictal central apnoea, providing human evidence of respiratory muscle atonia and supporting polygraphy for SUDEP risk assessment.

papers.title: EEG microstate alterations in psychotic depression: prolonged microstate C duration and associations with psychotic symptoms.
papers.summary: Compared resting-state EEG microstates in 68 patients with psychotic depression versus 63 with non-psychotic depression, finding prolonged microstate C duration and altered transition probabilities (increased B→A, decreased B→C and C→A) in the psychotic group, with reduced B→C transition most robustly associated with thought disturbance and hostility.

papers.title: Aperiodic neural activity predicts cortical excitability in TMS-EEG
papers.summary: Single-pulse TMS-EEG in healthy adults (n=29 M1, n=11 DLPFC) showed a strong negative relationship between the pre-stimulus aperiodic exponent and early local TMS-evoked potential amplitude in both regions, with steeper 1/f-like slopes associated with smaller EL-TEPs and inconsistent alpha/beta power relationships.

papers.title: A multiverse analysis of stomach-brain coupling in humans
papers.summary: Conducted a multiverse analysis of gastric-brain coupling using EEG and electrogastrography, systematically evaluating 5,184 unique analytic pipelines. Coupling magnitude varied with analytic decisions but remained relatively consistent at the group level across the parameter space, with coupling observed in alpha, theta, and beta bands, most prominently theta and beta and mainly at medial electrodes, alongside high inter-individual variance.

papers.title: Neural dynamics of emotionally expressive piano performance: a single-case study.
papers.summary: EEG recording of a concert pianist during a 27-minute performance revealed a stable left-lateralized fronto-striato-thalamic network across emotions, with emotion-specific modulations: Joy had highest subcortical activation, Melancholy showed right-hemisphere recruitment and lowest subcortical magnitude, and motor complexity correlated with activation in motor regions.

papers.title: Sensorimotor cortex activity during cued gait differs in Parkinson's freezers and non-freezers
papers.summary: Used mobile EEG to measure stride-locked sensorimotor beta (13-30 Hz) dynamics in 18 Parkinson's patients with freezing, 21 without freezing, and 19 healthy controls walking with auditory and visual cues. Parkinson's freezers showed smaller cue-related speed and stride-length gains, greater contralateral sensorimotor swing-phase beta suppression (most robust with visual cues), and an opposite association between beta suppression and gait improvement compared with non-freezers, suggesting distinct sensorimotor control mechanisms for cue utilization.

papers.title: Integrating task-state electroencephalography and motor function for intelligent assessment of recovery status from prolonged disorders of consciousness.
papers.summary: Built an intelligent assessment framework combining task-state ERP-derived alpha-band power spectral densities and coherence with motor function scores from 78 prolonged disorders of consciousness patients; linear SVM and logistic regression under leave-one-out cross-validation achieved macro-average F1 around 76% and AUC around 72-78%.

papers.title: Bridging language phenotypes, neural dynamics and gene regulation in autism.
papers.summary: This review proposes a neurophysiological imaging genetics framework that uses neural oscillatory profiles as endophenotypes linking autism risk genes to language deficits, and suggests neuromodulation as an experimental approach to investigate and modulate altered oscillatory dynamics in autism.

papers.title: Temporoparietal alpha dynamics shape feedback-based updating during social bargaining
papers.summary: Combining computational modeling, EEG, fMRI, diffusion MRI, and fMRI-guided rhythmic TMS across 296 sessions in 219 participants during repeated social bargaining, the study linked trial-by-trial feedback-based updating to alpha-beta dynamics and multivoxel representations in right temporoparietal cortex. Rhythmic alpha-TMS over individually localized TPJ selectively reduced feedback-based updating versus active arrhythmic stimulation, implicating a distributed temporoparietal-frontal network.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence applications in intracranial electroencephalography for epilepsy management: Insights from AI in Epilepsy 2025.
papers.summary: This review examines artificial intelligence applications to intracranial EEG (including stereo-EEG) for epilepsy management, covering epileptogenic zone localization, surgical outcome prediction, multimodal MRI integration, and optimization of iEEG-guided stimulation and neuromodulation. It reports that current evidence is largely preliminary, dominated by retrospective single-center studies lacking independent external validation, while highlighting multimodal data integration and continuous sensing as promising directions.

papers.title: [Neurophysiological differentiation of children with ADHD alone and ADHD comorbid with dyslexia: a P600-like component analysis].
papers.journal: Zhongguo dang dai er ke za zhi = Chinese journal of contemporary pediatrics
papers.summary: This prospective study compared P600-like event-related potential latency during a spatial N-back task in 66 children with ADHD alone versus ADHD comorbid with developmental dyslexia (ADHD+DD). P600-like latency at Pz under 1-back was significantly longer in ADHD+DD, discriminating the groups with an AUC of 0.804 (cut-off 688 ms, sensitivity 63.2%, specificity 96.4%), supporting it as a candidate neurophysiological marker for comorbid dyslexia.

papers.title: NeuroCodec: EEG-Guided Latent-Domain Generative Model for High-Fidelity Target Speaker Extraction
papers.summary: NeuroCodec is introduced as a generative EEG-guided target speaker extraction framework operating in the latent space of a neural audio codec, using graph convolutions for spatial EEG dependencies, attention-based cross-modal fusion, Mamba temporal modeling, and a six-phase training curriculum. It outperformed baselines on perceptual metrics, achieved a mean listening-experiment score of 82.24 versus 49.63 for M3ANet, enabled 44.1 kHz reconstruction up to 20 kHz, and was extended to a causal streaming formulation.

papers.title: Validating electrical stimulation through the somatosensory system: a perspective on mismatch negativity and auditory prostheses.
papers.summary: This perspective argues that the somatosensory system can serve as a platform to test whether electrical stimulation engages the brain's predictive processing, using mismatch negativity (MMN) to compare natural touch versus electrotactile stimulation and to inform cochlear implant research. It recommends alternative MMN paradigms (roving, omission, local-global) to disentangle prediction error from sensory adaptation, noting existing evidence remains limited to a single MEG study plus feature-specific CI findings.

papers.title: N-back electroencephalography asymmetry and peripheral immune cell subpopulation composition.
papers.summary: In 24 healthy young adults, this study tested associations between peripheral immune cell subpopulation proportions (estimated via DNA methylation) and EEG asymmetry during a 2-back working memory task. Theta asymmetry was associated with natural killer cell and CD4+ T cell proportions, and immune markers significantly predicted 2-back target accuracy across three regression models, though some correlations did not survive Bonferroni correction.

papers.title: Cooperative processing of visual threat across collicular pathways
papers.summary: Combining cell-type-specific inhibition, large-scale electrophysiology, and functional ultrasound imaging, the study shows that inhibiting either narrow-field or wide-field superior colliculus neurons impairs escape to overhead visual threats, so both parallel pathways contribute. Deeper-layer superior colliculus activity selectively represented escape-associated stimuli and predicted escape initiation and vigor, supporting a cooperative circuit architecture for visually evoked defensive behavior.

papers.title: EEG-defined differences in functional networks following beta-band transcranial alternating current stimulation in patients with disorders of consciousness: a pilot study.
papers.summary: Applied 30-minute frontal 20 Hz tACS (1 mA) to 28 patients with disorders of consciousness and used fNIRS to measure hemoglobin-based functional connectivity and graph-theoretical network properties before and after stimulation. tACS was associated with transient enhancement of frontal functional connectivity and acute network reorganization (increased clustering coefficient, global efficiency, and local efficiency; decreased path length) that resolved by the second post-stimulation measurement, with effects dependent on baseline vEEG pathology and Coma Recovery Scale-Revised scores correlating with connectivity and efficiency measures.

papers.title: Automated Interpretation of EEG Reports Using a Large Language Model with Structured Confidence Outputs
papers.summary: The study evaluated a grammar-constrained Mistral-7B LLM pipeline for extracting structured diagnostic labels and four-point confidence levels from unstructured EEG reports, compared against a second human annotator and classical NLP baselines, with a portability test using MedGemma. Mistral-7B achieved 96% Core Agreement with the reference annotator (second annotator 98%) and detected rare epileptiform abnormalities missed by baselines, supporting research annotation use without establishing clinical readiness.

papers.title: Behavioural expression of ictal embarrassment: a stereo-EEG case report.
papers.summary: This stereo-EEG case report describes a 40-year-old woman with drug-resistant focal epilepsy whose ictal embarrassment arose from seizure onset in the middle frontal gyrus bank of the superior frontal sulcus (F2sb) with propagation to dorsal anterior cingulate cortex and superior anterior insula. Electrical stimulation reproduced the seizure, but the full behavioral embarrassment repertoire emerged only in the standing position and was associated with reduced node strength in a frontal-cingulo-insular network, suggesting bodily context shapes its expression.

papers.title: Motor network neurophysiological (TMS-EEG) markers as predictors of outcomes of ventriculoperitoneal shunt sustained for over a year in normal pressure hydrocephalus.
papers.journal: Fluids and barriers of the CNS
papers.summary: Evaluated a TMS-evoked potential (TEP)-based assessment (Delphi-MD) for predicting sustained response to ventriculoperitoneal shunt in 41 patients with possible idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus, with 18 shunted patients followed over one year. Higher baseline M1L waveform adherence (WFA) distinguished responders from non-responders with ROC-AUC 0.935 and, at a LOOCV-derived cutoff, achieved 90.9% sensitivity, 85.7% specificity, and 88.9% accuracy, whereas the cerebrospinal fluid tap test did not predict shunt responsiveness.

papers.title: Frontal Asymmetry in Infancy: Predictive Utility for Distinct Patterns of Temperament.
papers.summary: In 82 mother-infant dyads, frontal EEG asymmetry during Toy Removal (but not Peek-a-Boo) predicted mother-reported Surgency/Positive Affectivity, driven by Smiling and Laughter (f2 = 0.31), and predicted Negative Emotionality via Sadness (f2 = 0.20). Findings were interpreted as most consistent with the capability model of lateralization.

papers.title: Serotonin Neurobiology and Artificial Intelligence-Driven Biomarker Detection in Affective Disorders: A Comprehensive Review.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes serotonin neurobiology in affective disorders—synthesis, receptor heterogeneity, transporter function, and systems-level interactions—and examines AI/machine-learning biomarker discovery from neuroimaging, electrophysiology, physiological and language data, plus emerging serotonin biosensors for real-time neurochemical monitoring.

papers.title: Psychedelics and Reward Processing: Before and After the 1970 Controlled Substances Act.
papers.summary: This narrative review traces psychedelic reward-processing research from before the 1970 Controlled Substances Act to the present, contrasting liability framing (misuse/dependence risk) with therapeutic framing and arguing that the field needs experimental programs bridging behavior, circuit signals, and longitudinal clinical endpoints in substance use disorder.

papers.title: Piezoelectric actuator-evoked mechano-gated currents in trigeminal neurons innervating the mouse temporomandibular joint.
papers.summary: Combining whole-cell patch-clamp electrophysiology with immunohistochemistry in retrogradely labeled mouse temporomandibular joint (TMJ)-innervating trigeminal ganglion neurons, the authors identified five neuronal groups, with only large-diameter A-nociceptors responding to piezoelectric actuator-evoked mechanical stimulation; no classical A-LTMRs were recorded.

papers.title: Reviewer Comment on Patrick et al. "Evaluating EEG Requisition Quality and Clinical Factors Influencing Outcomes: A Retrospective Audit".
papers.journal: The Canadian journal of neurological sciences. Le journal canadien des sciences neurologiques
papers.summary: This is a reviewer comment on Patrick et al.'s retrospective audit evaluating EEG requisition quality and clinical factors influencing outcomes; no abstract or findings are supplied.

papers.title: Indolizine-Based Small-Molecule Fluorescent Probes for Ex Vivo Imaging of Amyloid-β Plaques.
papers.summary: Synthesized a library of 49 indolizine derivatives and screened them on ex vivo brain sections from 5XFAD mice against 6E10 antibody reference, identifying five hit compounds (YIZ-20, YIZ-32, YIZ-36, YIZ-45, YIZ-47) whose fluorescence colocalized with amyloid-β plaques. The selected YIZ probes showed modestly reduced spectral overlap with the Hoechst channel versus thioflavin S, supporting indolizine as a scaffold for ex vivo Aβ plaque imaging.

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
